newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 18.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Wednesday:
** The Dow Jones industrial average ended off just 0.37 of a point at 5,888.83 on Tuesday after renewed expectations of an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve gripped Wall Street.
** Indonesia's Investment Minister, Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo, said the government might offer fiscal incentives for plantation firms in a bid to attract more investment in the agricultural sector.
** Indonesia's Surabaya Stock Exchange planned to launch automated remote trading from Thursday following approval by the Capital Market Supervisory Agency (Bapepam).

** The Jakarta Composite Index rose 7.54 points, or 1.36 percent, to close at 561.94 points on Tuesday on institutional buying of a few heavyweight stocks in late trade following support from regional markets.
** Brokers said players were expected to take profit on Wednesday following recent rises, but any possible falls were likely to be limited.
** On Wednesday, the Indonesian rupiah was at 2,320.10/20.50 in early trading against an opening of 2,321.00/22.00.
** Astra on fresh market talk of a possible takeover and rights issue.

** Summarecon on market talk that the property firm had secured a deal to build a toll road in West Java. The firm has denied the rumour, adding it's new apartment project in north Jakarta was a success.

** Bank Tiara and Bank Mashill on reports that the capital market supervisory agency (Bapepam) may approve the merger proposal between the two banks. Bank Tiara has denied the reports, saying there were no such plan.
** Pharmaceutical firm Kalbe Farma on reports that the firm planned to announce a stock split and to reduce its shareholding in subsidiary Igar Jaya.
